public_rationale: The May 6 reporting describes MAI-1 as a large internal Microsoft project intended to compete with leading models, including GPT-4. Mistral's earlier announcement confirms the partnership mentioned in the lead-in. This supports a development-and-positioning claim. It does not establish that MAI-1 had already matched GPT-4: the reports made its eventual use dependent on performance.
limitations: Support depends on reading compete as intended competitive positioning.
The detailed project reporting ultimately relies on The Information.
Reported parameter counts do not demonstrate equal capabilities.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Beyond partnering with Mistral, Microsoft is building a large model in-house that is big enough to compete directly with GPT-4.

statement.excerpt: Playing the field with Mistral wasn’t enough; now he is building a really big model, big enough to compete directly with GPT-4, internally:
statement.document_title: Microsoft and OpenAI’s increasingly complicated relationship

from_speaker: big enough to compete directly with GPT-4
our_interpretation: The claim concerns an internal development project reported on the publication date, so the target is the publicly reportable state on May 6, 2024.
Big enough to compete means a project positioned as a potential GPT-4-class competitor, not a released model with demonstrated benchmark parity.
No numerical size or performance threshold is supplied.
The attribution to The Information qualifies the evidence; it is not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable contemporaneous reporting identifies an internal Microsoft large-model project positioned to compete with GPT-4, with Microsoft's Mistral relationship established separately.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish that no such project existed, that it was solely an externally developed model, or that it was not intended to compete in GPT-4's class.

evidence.locator: First paragraph under Original article from May 6, 2024
evidence.explanation: The original article identifies MAI-1 as Microsoft's internal project and describes its intended competitive class. Its underlying source is The Information, rather than an independent technical evaluation.

evidence.locator: Final article paragraph before the reporting credits
evidence.explanation: Reuters describes MAI-1 as an in-house project and reports a planned scale of roughly 500 billion parameters. It also says the intended use depended on performance and that Microsoft declined comment, limiting any inference of proven parity.
Mistral's announcement establishes the earlier partnership referenced by Marcus. Its February event date makes it background to the May 6 development observation.
